items.title: Close the --seed non-finite determinism hole in pick()
items.acceptance: --seed Infinity and --seed -Infinity each return the identical aphorism on every run at exit 0, with the same filters applied
items.notes: CONDUCTOR-CONFIRMED defect (kickoff probe: 6 distinct aphorisms in 6 runs, exit 0). Resolution chosen: DETERMINISTIC PICK, not exit 2. Reasoning, judged against the SPEC's own rules: args.js already accepts Infinity as numeric (Number('Infinity') is not NaN) and the Domain rule promises determinism for --seed with no finiteness carve-out, so rejecting it would mean inventing a NEW undocumented validation rule rather than fixing the actual defect — which is that select.js gates its deterministic branch on Number.isFinite while toUint32Seed's IEEE-754 bit-fold already handles +/-Infinity deterministically. NaN stays exit 2 (parseSeedValue already rejects it) and that is correct and unchanged. Doc statement of this resolution belongs to I-3, which is why this item's files_hint is code+test only. NOT flagged route_class core despite playbook L-026: the allocator posture is trickle with allow_premium_pct 0 and opus at 96%, and gear 1's rule is S-effort sonnet builds — deliberately routing a 3-line fix to fable would spend premium the allocator has explicitly zeroed. || VERIFIED cycle 3 by the conductor with checks authored at verification time (the builder never saw them): full test_cmd 52/52 green, end-to-end CLI stability 1-distinct-of-8 for +Inf, -Inf, and +Inf under a --tag filter, and a discriminator that independently re-derived the expected corpus index for each seed (a degenerate index-pin would have passed the stability check alone). NaN contract and the unseeded random branch both confirmed unchanged. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-003-verify-I-1.txt

items.title: Settle the four doc/behaviour divergences identically in SPEC.md and README.md
items.acceptance: SPEC.md Domain rules and README.md state in matching wording: how --author matches, what --list does with --seed, what --list --json emits, and how a non-finite --seed behaves; and SPEC.md's OPEN AMBIGUITIES comment is gone rather than left open
items.notes: Four divergences, not three: the I-1 resolution is the fourth and is documented here rather than in I-1, keeping code and prose in separate file scopes. Documentation follows the SHIPPED behavior (--author is substring containment, case-insensitive) rather than changing behavior to match prose — changing the match semantics would be a user-visible behavior change, which the brief forbids. Depends on I-1 so the seed prose describes a resolution that has actually landed. || MEASURED EVIDENCE from I-2a (cycle 4) for divergence (c): mutant M16 rewrote --list --json from NDJSON to a single pretty-printed JSON array and the full 52-test suite stayed green, so that surface is completely unprotected today. It is deliberately NOT being hardened by I-2b/I-2c - no Domain rule describes the combination, so a test would freeze the current implementation and pre-empt this item. Settle the rule here first. || NEW measured evidence (cycle 5): the --list LINE FORMAT ("<text> — <author>", em dash, single line) is now pinned by the M13 order test but is stated by no Domain rule — the rules describe order and completeness of --list, never its rendering. Same shape of gap as M16: a test now enforces something the spec does not promise. I-3 should either write the rule or loosen the assertion to order-only. Do not silently leave the test as the de-facto spec. || CLOSED cycle 7, as a SUPERSET of the three divergences the SPEC named. Conductor rulings, all following SHIPPED behavior: (a) --author is substring containment, case-insensitive; (b) --tag is WHOLE-TAG membership (stated adjacent to (a) so the asymmetry is visible — it is the most confusable thing about the tool); (c) --list accepts a valid --seed and ignores it, exit 0; (d) --list --json is NDJSON, one object per line in corpus order, NOT a JSON array; (e) --list plain form is `<text> — <author>`, em dash U+2014, one line per entry — the cycle-5 gap where a test pinned what no rule promised, resolved by WRITING THE RULE rather than loosening the test, because --list output is a real piped-into contract; (f) --seed accepts every value Number() parses to non-NaN (negative, non-integer, +/-Infinity), all deterministic, NaN alone is exit 2. SPEC's OPEN AMBIGUITIES comment block deleted, not edited. README's brittle '48 tests' count replaced with a description of coverage. || VERIFIED cycle 7 by EXECUTING the shipped binary, never by reading the prose — a docs item whose claims are all behavioral is verifiable the same way a code item is. Harness .swarm/runs/cycle-007-verify-I-3.js (authored at verification time; the agent never saw it): 36/36 checks pass, evidence .swarm/runs/cycle-007-verify-I-3.txt. Four discriminators included so a degenerate implementation could not pass: partial-author result set must EQUAL the full-name set (kills an equality reading of (a)); default 2-line indented output must DIFFER from --list's 1-line form (proves (e) describes two genuinely distinct formats); 7 distinct seeds must reach 7 distinct aphorisms (a determinism check alone is satisfied by an always-same-entry stub); NDJSON first/last line must match corpus[0]/corpus[49] (order, not just parseability). Suite 58/58 green throughout; zero product code touched. CONDUCTOR PRECISION EDIT after the first harness run: the agent's '--list accepts --seed but ignores it' read as though ANY seed value were fine under --list, but the harness EDGE check proved `--list --seed abc` still exits 2. Both files now say 'accepts a valid --seed' and name the parse-failure carve-out. Nothing was weakened to open the gate — the edit made the prose match a measurement that had already passed.

items.acceptance: the HELP string describes --author as a substring match and --tag as a whole-tag match, in wording consistent with SPEC.md Domain rules and README.md, and the suite still passes
items.notes: FOUND cycle 7 while verifying I-3, and deliberately held OUT of I-3's scope: the HELP string lives in src/args.js, a product file, while I-3 was scoped to the two doc files, and mixing them would have broken the pairwise-disjoint file rule. HELP currently says '--author <name>  filter by author (case-insensitive)' and '--tag <tag>  filter by tag (case-insensitive)'. Neither line is FALSE — both flags are case-insensitive — but both are incomplete in exactly the way I-3 just closed elsewhere: they omit that --author is substring containment and --tag is whole-tag, which is the asymmetry users trip over. This is a third documentation surface that still carries the pre-I-3 wording. NOT a behavior change: only the help text's prose moves. Watch for a test that pins HELP content (I-2a mutated HELP and the sweep's notes should be consulted before editing) — if one exists it must be updated in the same item, and a green suite is part of the acceptance. || CLOSED cycle 8 as a SUPERSET of the two divergences this item named. Conductor pre-decided all wording against the shipped source and the landed I-3 rulings; the haiku agent transcribed, it decided nothing. Three HELP lines moved: --author now reads 'filter by author (substring match, case-insensitive)', --tag reads 'filter by tag (whole-tag, case-insensitive)' and sits adjacent so the asymmetry is readable at a glance, and --json reads 'output as JSON (single line, or NDJSON with --list)'. The --json line is the WIDENING, recorded as a decision rather than taken silently: it carried the identical pre-I-3 defect (a documentation surface describing only the non-list case), it lives in the same file and same edit, and drawing the scope line so as to leave one of three known incompletenesses standing in the very file being opened to fix that defect class would have been artificial. Harness .swarm/runs/cycle-008-verify-I-7.js, authored at verification time and never shown to the agent; evidence .swarm/runs/cycle-008-verify-I-7.txt, 35/35 pass. Two things needed proving and reading the diff proves neither. SCOPE: HELP sits in a PRODUCT file, so the harness split src/args.js at the template-literal boundary and byte-compared prologue (216 B) and epilogue (2631 B) against HEAD - identical, so parseArgs and every constant are provably untouched; the literal itself changed 362 -> 397 B, which also proves the item was not a no-op. TRUTH: every new phrase is a claim about runtime behaviour, so each was executed rather than read, with three discriminators - the partial-author result set must EQUAL the full-name set (kills an equality reading of 'substring'), --tag test must exit 1 while --tag testing exits 0 (kills a substring reading of 'whole-tag'), and bare --json must be exactly 1 line while --list --json is 50 (proves the one HELP line names two genuinely distinct shapes, not NDJSON-of-one). End-to-end check confirms the binary prints the EDITED constant, not a stale duplicate. Suite 58/58 green, unchanged from HEAD.

items.title: Harden --list --json now that a Domain rule finally describes it
items.acceptance: a test fails against mutant M16 (--list --json rewritten to emit one pretty-printed JSON array) and, when removed, lets M16 survive the rest of the suite
items.notes: UNBLOCKED BY I-3, and only by I-3. Cycle 4's mutation sweep measured M16 — rewriting --list --json from NDJSON to a single pretty-printed JSON array — as surviving the entire 52-test suite, i.e. that surface is completely unprotected. Cycle 4 classified it DEFERRED rather than HOLE for a specific reason: no Domain rule described the combination, so a test written then would have promoted the day's implementation to a promise and pre-empted the decision I-3 existed to make. I-3 has now MADE that decision (NDJSON, one object per line, corpus order, explicitly not an array), so the surface has a rule and the deferral is spent. Same twice-proven bar as I-2b/I-2c (playbook L-029): failable against M16 specifically, and attributable in the strict form — mutation applied with the new test filtered out must leave the pre-cycle baseline green. The exact M16 mutation is recorded in .swarm/runs/cycle-004-classification.md. M22 stays BOUNDARY and is still not to be hardened. || CLOSED cycle 9. One test added to test/cli.test.js: '--list --json emits newline-delimited JSON, one object per line, in corpus order'. It asserts three things a weaker test would not: line count EQUALS the filtered-set size (an equality, not the floor the pre-existing --list test used), every line parses STANDALONE as a JSON object with text/author/tags (no line of a multi-line array can), and the parsed texts match corpus order. Suite 58 -> 59. || VERIFIED cycle 9 by a conductor harness authored at verification time and never shown to the builder (.swarm/runs/cycle-009-verify-I-8.js, evidence .swarm/runs/cycle-009-verify-I-8.txt, 24/24 pass). Proven twice per L-029: FAILABLE (M16 applied -> fail=1 and the ONLY failing test is the new one) and ATTRIBUTABLE in the strict form (M16 applied + the new test filtered -> tests 58 / pass 58 / fail 0, exactly the pre-cycle baseline the harness re-measured from HEAD rather than took from the builder). Controls: DENOMINATOR (pattern removes exactly 1 of 59 against pristine source, 58 green), SKIP-SANITY (an unrelated mutation still fails under the same pattern), and MUTATION-APPLIED on every scratch copy -- the last one matters most, because a mutation that silently failed to apply would make the ATTRIBUTABLE check pass VACUOUSLY, which is a pass-shaped false result. Three DISCRIMINATORS the new test also kills: a COMPACT single-line JSON array (still valid JSON, still every entry in order), REVERSED NDJSON order, and TRUNCATED NDJSON with the last entry dropped. The latter two also trip the pre-existing M12/M13 --list tests, which is the expected length/order overlap cycle 5 recorded, not a defect -- the claim is that the NEW test is among the failures, and it is. Product tree byte-identical to HEAD (bin/aphorism.js, src/args.js, src/select.js, src/corpus.js all compared against HEAD); git diff --name-only HEAD = test/cli.test.js alone. The I-2 hardening thread is now complete: every HOLE survivor from cycle 4's sweep is closed, and M22 remains BOUNDARY and unhardened as classified.

items.title: Corpus attribution triage (umbrella — decomposed cycle 10 into I-4a + I-4b)
items.acceptance: a written risk-ranked list names the corpus entries most likely to carry a wrong or unverifiable attribution with a stated reason each, and no file in the repo describes the corpus as audited, verified, or fact-checked
items.notes: TRIAGE, never an audit — nothing here can be confirmed without sources this run cannot reach, and the deliverable is explicitly a list for a human to settle (KI-2, T-006). Rank by internally-observable risk signals only: folklore maxims historically credited to several different people, wording that looks paraphrased or compressed rather than verbatim, entries already hedged as Anonymous (lowest risk, already honest), and entries traceable to a specific well-documented publication (lower risk). The stress-test's demo-embarrassment lens put this ABOVE the test items in value: a programming-aphorism CLI with misattributed quotes fails in exactly the way a green suite cannot see. || DECOMPOSED cycle 10 into I-4a and I-4b, per the cycle-9 handoff's stated preference for S-effort slices over accepting one M-effort exception under gear 1. The split is NOT by risk band, which would have been circular — you cannot slice by a ranking the work exists to produce. It is by KIND of claim: I-4b is the ranked judgment artifact (what is likely wrong), I-4a is a mechanical repo sweep (does any file overclaim). Those need different evidence and different verification, which is what makes the seam real. This umbrella closes when I-4a lands; id retired from direct execution, not dropped. || UMBRELLA CLOSED cycle 11 — both acceptance clauses verified, each with its own evidence. Clause 1 (risk-ranked list with a stated reason each) closed by I-4b cycle 10. Clause 2 (no file describes the corpus as audited/verified/fact-checked) closed by I-4a cycle 11 and verified by a REPO-WIDE sweep over all 9 product files, not just the edited one. Method note worth keeping: the first sweep returned "0 hits" and was DISCARDED rather than banked, because its negative control did not fire — the detector could not even find the text I had just deleted ("honest // attribution" defeated \s+ across the comment marker). The rewritten detector fires on the exact old header plus two synthetic overclaims, and only then was its 0-hit result admitted as evidence. A zero from a detector that has not been shown to be capable of a one is not a zero.

items.notes: The other half of I-4's acceptance clause. CONDUCTOR-SCOUTED cycle 10, not yet executed: a grep across README.md, REPORT.md and src/ found REPORT.md already honest (it states the attributions are unaudited and KI-2 open), but src/corpus.js carries a header comment claiming 'honest attribution' and that uncertain entries 'are attributed to Anonymous rather than guessing a famous name'. Ordered AFTER I-4b deliberately — the triage supplies the evidence for what the replacement wording may honestly say, and doing it first would have meant writing the comment twice. Conductor-executed and S-effort: it is a prose edit to a product file, which by the cycle-8 precedent must be gated by byte-comparing everything outside the edited comment against HEAD. || DONE cycle 11, conductor-executed. Two edits, both prose: (1) src/corpus.js header — the claim "honest attribution" and the policy sentence "where the true author is uncertain ... the entry is attributed to Anonymous rather than guessing a famous name" were REMOVED, not softened, because I-4b measured them false (1 of 50 hedged to Anonymous vs 8 HIGH-risk entries all naming famous people: Knuth, Karlton, Dijkstra, Beck, Wheeler, Hopper, Stroustrup, Kay). Restating a policy the file does not follow, in weaker words, would still have been fiction. Replacement states attribution is UNVERIFIED and points at the triage. items.title: Make the Attribution count extraction robust to digits reordered within one clause
items.acceptance: Rewording the Attribution sentence so that a different CORRECT digit sits nearer the HIGH marker than the HIGH count itself -- e.g. `8 of the 50 entries carry a rating of HIGH` -- leaves the suite GREEN, while the same reworded prose carrying a WRONG HIGH count still fails. Proven twice per L-029.
items.notes:
Source: conductor probe N1, cycle 22 -- .swarm/runs/cycle-022-verify-T-016.txt. MEASURED, not suspected: rewriting the Attribution aside as `covers every entry. 8 of the 50 entries carry a rating of HIGH, and it says what would settle each one.` -- with every number still TRUE -- fails the suite at 71/70/1, naming the C2 test. Cause: extractNearestPrecedingCount splits the section on em/en dashes and then takes the digit run NEAREST BEFORE the marker within that clause; with the dashes gone the whole paragraph collapses into one clause, and in that word order 50 sits nearer to HIGH than 8 does. The builder flagged exactly this edge case in its own report rather than hiding it, which is the only reason it was probed -- an honest uncertainty report converted directly into a measured backlog item. IMPORTANT, and the reason this is LOW value rather than a repeat of T-012: the guard does NOT go quiet. It fails LOUD and names the claim, so a maintainer who trips it is told exactly what happened. This is a false REJECTION of an honest edit -- the safe direction -- and it gets the same classification T-018 got at cycle 20 for the same reason. Fix shape: bind the digit to its marker by proximity in BOTH directions within the clause, or match the two claims as a pair (`N ... entries` and `M ... HIGH`), rather than assuming the README will keep using dash-delimited asides. Source: conductor gate cell N1, cycle 30 (.swarm/runs/cycle-030-verify-T-021.txt). This repo's standing classification is that loud-and-wrong is the safe direction and silent-and-wrong is the failure class the run exists to remove, so trading a silent hole for a loud rejection is the correct direction of travel even though it is a new rejection. The failure is also maximally informative: the assert names both offending headings verbatim and says it is refusing to pick one.\n\nJUDGMENT FLAG: it is genuinely arguable that a README with two headings both claiming to describe --list behaviour is AMBIGUOUS DOCUMENTATION and that failing loud is correct behaviour rather than a defect -- in which case the right outcome is to close this item with that reasoning recorded and no code change. That is the conductor's current lean; it is filed rather than decided so the alternative gets a measurement instead of an assertion.

CYCLE 33 -- DECIDED **STAY RED**, closed as a deliberate accepted trade, no code change. The item demanded measurement rather than argument, and the conductor's recorded lean is now backed by a cell rather than being adopted on its own say-so.

MEASURED: the strongest NON-POSITIONAL disambiguator available -- keep only those candidate sections whose own body carries a `<text>...<author>` format literal (arm F_CONTENT; not first-match, not last-match, it reads content) -- was implemented and run against the theft shape. Cell V7 plants a decoy section carrying a CORRECT-looking literal while the REAL section's literal is mutated so it no longer parses as a literal at all. HEAD catches that README (78/77/1). F_CONTENT goes **GREEN on it (78/78/0)** -- it picks the decoy and the real section's wrong literal is never examined. So the disambiguation that would make this item green buys that green by reintroducing the cycle-28 SILENT hole, in non-positional clothing. V5:F_CONTENT confirms the item's goal is reachable (78/78/0) -- the two cells together are the whole trade, stated in outputs rather than in prose.

CONCLUSION: two "### " headings both claiming to describe --list behaviour ARE ambiguous documentation, and refusing to pick one while naming both verbatim is correct behaviour, not a defect. Loud-and-wrong stays the accepted direction; silent-and-wrong is the class this run exists to remove.

CYCLE 33 CORROBORATION, INDEPENDENT AND BY A DIFFERENT ROUTE. The dispatched classifier reached STAY-RED separately, refuting a DIFFERENT candidate than the conductor did. The conductor built a CONTENT-based disambiguator (prefer the candidate whose section carries a format literal) and measured it GREEN on a theft README the current code catches.
